# Bregman records, original facet complements, and an actual convex-order obstruction

This combines the finite sampled-facet partition with the ACTUAL h-scale
normal Bregman and chi records. Two different losses must be distinguished.
Saturated infinite offsets can carry original complementary area that is
invisible to both records. Even when all offsets are the unsaturated value
-1/2, the records do not imply ordinary convex order between the original
inside/outside slice measures, or between their complementary layers.
The second assertion below has an actual all-normal deepest-source and
minimizing-cap certificate, rather than merely compatible roof provenance.

No example here is a global bad-body minimum or below the OC target.
No obstruction to every possible source-anchored transport is claimed.

## 1. The exact symmetry and what the finite partition preserves

Write Psi(q)=clamp(1+q,0,1),

    J(q)=((q+1)_+^2-q_+^2)/2,
    B(q,s)=J(q+s)-J(q)-Psi(q)s.

Then

    Psi(-1-q)=1-Psi(q),
    B(-1-q,-s)=B(q,s).                              (1)

The latter follows either from the first identity by differentiation in
s, with both sides zero at s=0, or directly from J. In particular
B(-1/2,s) is EVEN in s. At q=+-infinity the compactified cost is zero
for every finite s. The transition density chi is also zero there.

On an outside facet W=tau, whereas on an inside facet W=1-tau. Thus
paired points w_out,w_in satisfying

    w_in=2*barY-w_out, q_in=-1-q_out                 (2)

have the same tau and exactly the same Bregman cost for EVERY simultaneous
normal test k_D(w)=D.(w-barY). Their chi-weighted quadratics also agree
when their endpoint records are paired. This is one joint geometric
identity, not a different coupling chosen for each D.

The finite perturbation partition of
`candidate 71864c461210d110`
can be applied to the limiting ambient supporting facets, while the
records are restricted from the SAME sequence of actual nearby roofs.
There are only finitely many sampled bases, so the fixed tie assignment
does not split or change any selected base's original trace or offset
record. All Bregman and chi integrals decompose additively over those
pieces. Their inequalities do NOT thereby become separate inequalities
on each piece. In particular (2) can couple two different ambient facets
and two different lower-rank incidence pieces.

The complementary original trace remains

    dC=(1-tau)dA.                                    (3)

For another proper cap H its exact retained load is int_H dC, in
addition to the selector lift contribution int_H tau dA. The comparison
cost B depends on the original scaled offset q and the normal displacement;
it is not the integral of a fixed convex function against (3).

## 2. One actual roof sequence: tau=(1-x^2)_+ and invisible complements

Fix R>=2, L->infinity, and H=L^(-2). Define the even concave roof on
[-R,R]

    r_L(x)=-x^2                         if |x|<=1,
           -1-L(|x|-1)                 if 1<=|x|<=R. (4)

For L>=2 the one-sided derivative jumps in the correct concave direction.
At integer bases -1,0,+1 in n=1,d=2 prescribe

    K_-={(x,t): |x|<=R, -1<=t<=H(1/2+r_L(x))},
    K_+=-K_-,
    K_0=[-R,R] x [H/2-R,H/2+R].                     (5)

For large L these are positive convex fibers. The average of the two
outer fibers lies in [-R,R]x[-1,1], hence in K_0. Their canonical convex
hull has exactly the prescribed complete three-fiber sample. This is
ONE sequence of actual convex bodies, including both boundary bases.

Let Sigma_L be its actual pooled within-fiber covariance. It is diagonal
by x-reflection. Set sigma_L=sqrt(Sigma_tt), c_L=sqrt(Sigma_xx/Sigma_tt),
and use the actual normalized smoothing parameter h_L=H/sigma_L. At
source Y_L=(0,H/2), the positive vertical cap has kernel (t-H/2)/H.
On the limiting outer supporting facets t=0 its raw roof arguments are

    q_out=r_L(x), q_in=-1-r_L(-x).                    (6)

Consequently tau_out=tau_in=(1-x^2)_+ exactly, while their limiting records
are

    q_out=-x^2, q_in=x^2-1, chi=1        on |x|<1;
    q_out=-infinity, q_in=+infinity, chi=0 on 1<|x|<=R. (7)

The physical points (-1,x,0) and (+1,-x,0) are reflected through the
limiting source. Equation (1) gives EQUALITY in every full-normal Bregman
comparison and in the chi PSD comparison. It also gives equality in
the old unrestricted absolute-incidence quota. Proper middle sections
contribute zero to the h-scale Bregman limit, as in the proved theorem.

On each outer facet the original area, selector mass and complement mass
are respectively

    A=2R, |L_tau|=4/3, |C_tau|=2R-4/3.               (8)

For the proper halfspace x>=0 these are R,2/3,R-2/3. Of the complement
mass in (8), exactly 2(R-1) lies on infinite-offset patches unseen by
B and chi. The finite-offset core contributes the remaining 2/3.
This proper halfspace tests the exact load identity; it is not asserted
to be a member of the rank-one active menu certified below.
The unit-prism complement is still nonconvex: for R=1 it contains the
points (-1,1/2),(1,1/2), while their midpoint (0,1/2) is absent. The
actual convex selector lift uses its genuine projection [-1,1]; it does
not append zero-height traces over 1<|x|<=R. Its vertical lengths
extended by zero still equal tau, so (8) and all load integrals hold.

After canceling the same per-cap coarea factor, all Bregman/chi costs in
this family are independent of R: they are supported on |x|<1. Original
complement mass can grow without bound. Thus these costs alone cannot
bound the ORIGINAL complementary cost by a numerical multiple of the
finite-record cost. Changing R also changes other global body data; this
is not a counterexample to a theorem that uses those additional data.

### 2a. In fact this selected cap is an actual all-normal minimum

This is stronger than needed for the invisibility assertion. Here are
the details, so the finite-width claim is not silently assumed.

The limiting covariance ratio is

    c_R^2=4R^2(R+1)/(4R^3+1)>1.                     (9)

Indeed the middle mass is 4R^2, the total outer mass tends to4R,
Sigma_xx tends to R^2/3, and Sigma_tt tends to
(4R^3+1)/(12(R+1)). The middle's translation does not affect its own
covariance. Thus c_L stays in a fixed compact interval [c_-,c_+] with
c_->1 for large L.

For ANY base tilt a and continuous normal (b,+1), paired outer points
have kernel arguments whose sum is

    -1/sqrt(1+c_L^2 b^2) >= -1.

Their captures therefore sum to at least1. The whole outer capture is
at least V_L=|K_-|. For (b,-1) the sum is positive, and for a horizontal
normal it is0, so the same quota holds for EVERY continuous orientation.
For b=0,+1 it is exactly V_L for EVERY base tilt.

It remains to bound the middle rectangle's own centered smoothing gain.
For normal (b,1) put w=H sqrt(1+c_L^2 b^2) and m=R max(1,|b|).
Its projection density f_b satisfies

    f_b(0)=2R/max(1,|b|),
    f_b(s)>=f_b(0)(1-s/m) for 0<=s<=m.              (10)

These follow directly from convolution of two centered interval laws.
If |b|<=1/2 and w<=R/2, the full transition is in the central plateau,
so its gain over half-volume is exactly Rw>=RH. If |b|>=1/2, integration
of (10) gives gain divided by RH at least

    G(b)[1-H G(b)/(3R)],
    G(b)=sqrt(1+c_L^2 b^2)/max(1,|b|).

Here G>=kappa=min{sqrt(1+c_-^2/4),c_-}>1 and
G<=K=sqrt(1+c_+^2). For sufficiently small H,
kappa(1-HK/(3R))>1. The horizontal limit gives gain RH c_L>RH.
The rectangle is centrally symmetric, so both normal signs obey this
bound. Its least centered capture is therefore exactly 2R^2+RH.

Every cap at Y_L consequently has mass at least

    Q_L=V_L+2R^2+RH,                                (11)

attained by the positive vertical cap. A sufficiently large generic
base tilt also makes the negative vertical cap attain it, by fully
capturing one outer fiber and missing the other.

For a middle mark with vertical displacement s from H/2, one such
isolating tilt gives depth at most V_L+2R^2+RH-2R|s|. At height H/2
but horizontal coordinate x0!=0, the untilted positive vertical cap has
mass Q_L, but its derivative in the transverse normal b is nonzero:
the section's x moment is0 and the through-mark derivative is -x0 times
its positive section mass. The width derivative is0 because Sigma_xt=0.
Hence its depth is strictly less than Q_L. Endpoint bases can be exposed
and isolated, giving depth at most V_L<Q_L. Pure-base closed caps through
0 have mass at least4R^2+V_L>Q_L. Thus Y_L is the actual UNIQUE global
deepest source. The positive and a suitably tilted negative vertical cap
form an actual balanced rank-one menu. No full-rank bad-menu claim follows.

## 3. Actual half-selected example: no convex order even with all offsets finite

There is a simpler exact example which rules out a universal ordinary
convex-order comparison of the ORIGINAL slice measures. Use n=2,d=1,

    p1=(1,0), p2=(0,1), p3=(-1,-1),
    P={0,+-p1,+-p2,+-p3}.

Their hexagon has exactly these seven lattice points. Put an interval
[-1,0] at every p_j and [0,1] at every -p_j. At0 put

    K_0=[H/2-B,H/2+B], B>=2, 0<H<1.

The six outer bases are exposed vertices. Every convex combination of
outer points at base0 lies in [-1,1], which is contained in K_0. Thus
the canonical hull has these exact fibers and is lattice-complete.

Let sigma be its pooled within-fiber standard deviation and h=H/sigma.
At Y=H/2 the positive continuous cap has kernel

    Psi((t+a.z-H/2)/H).

Pair (p_j,t) with (-p_j,-t). Their arguments sum exactly -1, so outer
capture is exactly3 for EVERY a. The middle capture is B+H/2. Negative
continuous caps have paired arguments summing+1, so outer capture is
at least3; a large generic base tilt saturates one member of every pair
and attains3. There are only these two continuous orientations in d=1.
Pure-base caps through0 contain K_0 and at least three outer fibers.
The same isolating-tilt upper bound at every other middle mark and the
exposed outer-base bound prove an actual UNIQUE global deepest source,

    Q=B+3+H/2, M=2B+6.

An actual balanced menu consists of the untilted positive cap and a
large-tilt negative cap. The untilted cap's supporting traces have

    q=-1/2, tau=1/2, chi=1

at all six outer bases. There are three outside and three inside
supports. Their Bregman comparison is equality for EVERY D and t by
B(-1/2,s)=B(-1/2,-s). The chi, unrestricted squared/absolute incidence,
and uniform-kernel signed tau(1-tau) budgets are also equality.

The complementary original slice measures are

    mu_out=(1/2) sum_j delta_(p_j),
    mu_in =(1/2) sum_j delta_(-p_j).                 (12)

They have equal mass3/2 and equal first moment0. Nevertheless neither
dominates the other in convex order. The convex physical functions

    Phi_+(z)=(z1+z2-1)_+,
    Phi_-(z)=(-z1-z2-1)_+

give respectively

    int Phi_+ dmu_out=0,   int Phi_+ dmu_in=1/2;
    int Phi_- dmu_out=1/2, int Phi_- dmu_in=0.        (13)

Therefore there is NO martingale coupling in either direction between
these original complementary measures. The same is true for the full
original supporting measures and for the selector layers, by scaling.
This conclusion uses only the necessary Jensen implication of a
martingale, so no external transport theorem is needed.

Each supporting incidence lies in a legitimate lower-base-rank piece
of the finite ambient-facet cover. Keeping the original labels and
actual offsets does not repair (13). The failure is not due to a
discarded boundary base, a different roof sequence, saturation, missing
normal stationarity, or an arbitrary noncritical menu.

There IS the deterministic reflection coupling z->-z. Its conditional
barycenter is -z, not z. Such a source-anchored coupling may be useful,
but is a different statement from ordinary convex order. This example
does not obstruct that more flexible possibility or a global payment
using the second actual menu cap. Its normalized depth tends to1/2,
well above the n=2,d=1 target1/8.

## 4. Exact scope of the two tests

The original tau=1-x^2 complement survives even under one coherent
body sequence and an actual all-normal cap minimum. Its finite record
sees neither the saturated tail area nor its proper-cap loads. In the
half-selected example every offset is finite, but even the FULL family
of normal Bregman tests cannot be upgraded to arbitrary convex tests of
the original lower-rank base measures: the exact hinges (13) obstruct it.

Thus the finite facet partition and the actual Bregman/chi comparison do
not, by themselves, give the proposed ordinary convex-order pairing or
a bound on the complementary-layer cost. A successful further step
must retain another ingredient, such as a source-anchored reflected
transport, the other cap loads, or the global physical-field separator.
No induction or Gamma payment is concluded from these two inputs alone.
